The Chief Executive’s Report for South Dublin County Council is presented to elected members at each 
monthly Council meeting.  Section 136(2) of the Local Government Act 2001, as inserted by Section 
51 of the Local Government Reform Act 2014, requires the Chief Executive to prepare a management 
report in relation to the performance of executive functions, including implementation of policy or other 
matters required by the Council in the exercise of its reserved functions, and the provision of services. 
It should be viewed in conjunction with the various updates provided to Area Committee Meetings as 
well as the quarterly Capital Progress Report to full Council as part of the reporting structures to assist 
the elected members with their governance and oversight responsibilities.
The report includes important updates and information from across our various directorates and 
departments together with a range of key statistics that were developed in conjunction with the elected 
members.  It provides the opportunity to highlight major news events and to focus on different areas 
of our work that may not always get the attention it deserves while a selection of images from recent 
events is also included.

Safe Routes to School  
Monastery Road Wall Repair
Work continues by our Active 
Travel team to improve safety on 
main access routes to schools. Six 
schools in South Dublin County 
were included in Round 3 of the 
Safe Routes to Schools (SRTS) 
programme that was published by 
the NTA and An Taisce in 2024.  
Travel surveys and front-of-school 
audits have been completed for four 
schools so far, and the remaining 
two will be completed this month. 
Once all audits are finished, we 
will prepare outline delivery plans 
for each school. These plans will 
recommend measures to improve 
safety at school gates and along 
main access routes, and we will 
begin progressing the design work 
later this year
We have also provided additional 
funding for a supplementary Safe 
School Zones programme.  This will 
see safety measures provided at 
further schools across the county, 
with front-of-school assessments 
and travel surveys conducted at 
eight schools and safety works 
proposed for four schools so far 
this year.
Tallaght LAP Extended 
An extension to Tallaght Town Centre 
Local Area Plan (LAP) was approved at 
the council meeting in April meeting to 
align the LAP timeframes with the County 
Development Plan up to 2028.  With the 
LAP originally set to lapse in 2026, the 
extension ensures a consistent policy 
framework for Tallaght. To date, under 
the LAP which was approved in 2020, 
there has been significant investment 
by the council, supported by the 
government’s Urban Regeneration and 
Development Fund (URDF), to provide 
major public realm enhancements, an 
innovation centre and expansion of 
Tallaght Stadium along with the start of 
redevelopment of Cookstown and Airton, 
as the regeneration of Tallaght Town 
Centre progresses.
“Think Twice – Think Bike” Motorcyclist Road Safety Campaign Launched
Major wall repairs completed at 
Monastery Road.
Palmerstown Safe School Zone 
Our latest road safety initiative sees 
us 
partner 
with 
An 
Garda 
Síochána and neighbouring local 
authorities 
to 
launch the ‘Think 
Twice, Think Bike’ campaign.  
This involves radio & social media 
campaigns to highlight to motor 
cyclists 
the 
dangers 
they 
face, 
particularly 
as 
summer 
approaches 
when 
more 
motorcyclists take to the roads.
It was launched at the May Bank 
Holiday 
weekend 
to 
encourage 
safer road use and 
to 
highlight 
’safe 
ways’ 
for 
motorcyclists 
to 
protect 
themselves. 
 
Motorcyclists 
are 
vulnerable road users with RSA 
data showing that 105 motorcyclists 
were fatally injured, and 921 were 
seriously injured between 2019 and 
2023.
At the launch, our Road Safety Officer 
Orlaith Maguire said ‘the campaign 
targets both motorcyclists and car 
drivers to focus on the safety of 
motorcycles on our roads. Research 
shows that almost 51% of fatalities 
occur at weekends and so far this 
year there have been 10 motor cyclist 
fatalities on Irish roads.  
It takes a split second to change 
someone’s life forever, and as a driver 
you have to ask yourself could you 
live with the consequence of your 
actions? We all share the road, so 
let’s all come together to make that 
safer for motorcyclists and all road 
users.”
This latest campaign follows three 
previous initiatives this year: safe 
use of e-scooters, National Slowdown 
Day and National Tyre Safety Day and 
further details of each can be found 
at www.sdcc.ie
In January Storm Eowyn caused 
significant damage around the 
county, notably at Monastery 
Road where an old mature tree 
fell causing major damage by 
knocking down six meters of 
stone wall at Monastery Rise.
We appointed Truir Construction 
to carry out specialist repair 
work to the wall, with craft 
stonemasons engaged to carry 
out the works.  
As much of the original stone 
was used as possible along 
with traditional lime mortar and 
locally salvaged stone from our 
Corkagh Park depot to ensure 
that the repaired wall, which is 
now successfully completed, is in 
keeping with the original design.

Launch of Affordable Homes at Canal Bank, Clonburris
60 new affordable homes at Canal 
Bank within the Clonburris Strategic 
Development Zone will be launched 
for sale later this month by SDCC.  
These homes, ranging from one to 
four bedrooms in size, will be made 
available to eligible applicants under 
the Affordable Purchase Scheme.
Thie development at Canal Bank 
marks our first directly contracted 
delivery of affordable homes in many 
years, supporting increased affordable 
housing options under the national 
housing policy, Housing for All.
Canal Bank is a brand-new development 
of 116 social and affordable homes 
that is located adjacent to the Grand 
Canal near the heart of Clonburris, 
West Dublin’s newest town.  
It offers an excellent selection of high-
quality homes in a mix of houses, 
apartments and duplexes.  Designed 
to feature parks, play areas, dedicated 
biodiversity 
areas, 
walkways 
and 
cycle paths, as well as new retail and 
commercial hubs, the new community 
of Clonburris will provide an urban 
living environment which will have 
new schools, community space, creches 
and which is also just minutes from 
Dublin city centre with Clonburris train 
station within easy walking distance.
The development is scheduled for 
completion by November of this year 
and so the 60 affordable purchase 
homes will be launched for sale in a 
single phase with the following  home 
types available:
•	
8 x one-bedroom apartments
•	
18 x two-bedroom apartments

New Maker in Residence William Davis
Nigerian theatre and filmmaker Newton 
Barabara collaborated with residents of 
the IPAS Centres—The Towers, Dolcain 
House, and the Red Cow Hotel—between 
January and April 2025. Barabara, a firm 
believer in the transformative power of 
storytelling, aimed to build community 
and encourage cultural exchange. 
During the workshops, participants 
engaged in storytelling, role-play, 
acting, scriptwriting, and character 
development.
They worked alongside acclaimed 
practitioners Veronica Coburn and 
Phil Kingston, Head of Education at 
the Abbey Theatre. The sessions were 
designed to boost creativity, teamwork, 
and 
confidence. 
This 
programme 
builds on Barabara’s earlier work at 
the Citywest Transition Hub, which 
concluded with a public performance of 
the play Halfway to Heaven in 2024. The 
residency culminated in The Journey, a 
powerful original play that confronts 
the emotional aftermath of trauma and 
the urgent instinct to survive.
Set 
against 
the 
backdrop 
of 
displacement, the story explores how 
hardship tests human relationships, 
challenging trust, love, and identity. 
Through the harrowing path of its 
central character, we witness both 
heartbreak and resilience as they 
navigate fear, sacrifice, and fleeting 
moments of connection.
Newton Barabara aims for the play to 
stir deep reflection on the universal 
human experiences of loss, longing, and 
the pursuit of belonging. The Journey 
shines a light on the courage it takes 
to start over—and the unbreakable 
hope that carries us forward. Supported 
by the Arts Council and South Dublin 
County Council, in partnership with The 
Abbey Theatre Education Department.

Templeogue College School Visit
Cyber Awareness Week for Staff
On April 29th, 21 students from 
Templeogue College who were 
elected to represent their classes 
visited the council chamber with 
their teacher, Mr Séamus Connor. 
They 
met 
the 
Mayor, 
elected 
members, and staff from South 
Dublin County Council.
During 
the 
visit, 
the 
student 
representatives 
heard 
from 
Councillors about how to effectively 
represent their classmates and why 
local democracy matters. They met 
the Returning Officer in the 2019 and 
2024 local elections, Lorna Maxwell, 
who spoke about the proportional 
representation election system that 
is used in Ireland.  
The visit was designed to help 
the next generation of voters 
understand how Ireland’s voting 
system works and why it’s important 
to use their right to vote. All schools 
in the county are welcome to 
engage with the Council to learn 
more about democracy and the 
importance of using your vote in all 
elections.  
Cardiff Council Workshop
The four Dublin local authorities recently 
held a workshop with Ffionn Gruffudd 
from Cardiff Council, joined by members of 
the Irish language community. The event 
included a panel discussion with community 
representatives, chaired by Kathy Scott from 
the Trailblazery.
Ffionn Gruffudd, representing Bilingual 
Cardiff, shared valuable insights on how 
Cardiff Council has worked to meet Welsh 
language standards. Given the similarities 
between the Irish and Welsh languages, the 
Welsh experience could help guide our own 
efforts to meet Irish language targets.
The workshop ended with a discussion 
on recruitment goals—looking at what 
lessons from Cardiff’s approach apply to 
us, the challenges we may face, and the 
opportunities and actions we can focus on 
moving forward.
Strategic Workforce Development Plan 2025-2029
Cyber talks to build a “Human Firewall”
As part of its ongoing commitment to 
digital safety, our IT Department hosted 
a series of Cyber Awareness events 
from 7th - 11th April. These sessions 
aimed to strengthen staff knowledge 
around cybersecurity and highlight 
the important role everyone plays in 
protecting the Council’s digital systems. 
Over 170 staff members—including 
the Senior Management Team—took 
part in five informal coffee morning 
sessions. These engaging talks focused 
on key cyber risks and how staff can act 
as a “human firewall” to help prevent 
threats. Staff were reminded to report 
any suspicious activity promptly to 
ensure a fast and effective response. 
We look forward to continuing this 
important conversation during Cyber 
Month 2025, taking place this October.
Students from Templeogue College in the Council Chamber
Through extensive consultation and 
collaboration across all levels of the 
organisation, we have successfully 
developed 
a 
comprehensive 
Strategic Workforce Development 
Plan for the period 2025 to 2029. 
This forward-looking plan is designed 
to strengthen workforce capabilities, 
ensuring they are fully aligned with 
the evolving goals and strategic 
direction 
of 
the 
organisation. 
 
At its core, the plan adopts a holistic 
approach to recruitment, retention, 
and 
employee 
development. 
It 
places 
strong 
emphasis 
on 
creating 
a 
flexible, 
inclusive, 
and 
modern 
hybrid 
working 
environment. A key focus is also on 
enhancing 
recruitment 
practices 
to attract top talent, while actively 
promoting SDCC as an employer 
of choice within the public sector. 
The development of this plan 
was underpinned by a detailed 
analysis of both current workforce 
requirements and future demands. It 
identifies the critical people, skills, 
and resources that will be necessary 
to 
meet 
emerging 
challenges 
and deliver on our objectives. 
 
Among the key actions outlined are 
the formulation of a comprehensive 
People Strategy, a robust Learning 
and Development Strategy, and 
the 
expansion 
of 
the 
existing 
Staff Wellbeing Programme. These 
initiatives are designed to support 
a high-performing, agile workforce. 
 
Crucially, the plan highlights the 
importance of diversity, inclusion, and 
continuous innovation. By investing 
in its people and leveraging data-
driven insights, SDCC is committed 
to delivering exceptional public 
services while cultivating a resilient 
culture of engagement, creativity, 
and collaboration.

Dublin Climate Action Week 
(#DCAW25) 2025
Supporting Waste Enforcement 
During the week commencing 12th May, 
we are delighted to host a programme 
of events to mark Dublin Climate Action 
Week 2025.  A rich and varied schedule is 
running across the Dublin region to inform, 
engage and inspire climate action across 
communities with selected highlights that 
include guided nature walks, interactive 
workshops, family fun days, expert-led 
sessions and much more.
Dublin Climate Action Week 2025 is 
being organised and delivered by SDCC 
in partnership with our local authority 
colleagues in Dublin City Council, Dún 
Laoghaire-Rathdown County Council and 
Fingal County Council as well as partner 
agencies 
including 
Codema–Dublin’s 
Energy Agency and the Dublin Metropolitan 
Climate Action Regional Office (DM CARO).
Whether you’re passionate about climate 
action, curious to learn more or simply 
looking for ways to connect with your 
local community, there will be many 
opportunities to participate. 
Both the event schedule and online 
registration 
are 
available 
at 
www.
dublinclimateactionweek.ie while everyone 
can also keep up to date across the week 
by using the #DCAW25 hashtag on social 
media.
Park Rangers Guided Walks in 
Tymon and Dodder Valley Parks
For the upcoming National Biodiversity 
Week and National Pollinator Week, our park 
rangers will lead guided walks in Tymon 
Park and Dodder Valley Park, showcasing 
local flora, fauna, and recent pollinator 
friendly enhancements. The walks will take 
place during Biodiversity Week in May and 
Pollinator Week in June, and are scheduled 
for:
20th May:  Tymon (11:00am) & Dodder 
Valley (2:00pm)
17th June:  Tymon (11:00am) & Dodder 
Valley (2:00pm).
Meeting points are: Tymon Park Rangers 
Office (53°18’00.6”N 6°20’30.0”W) and 
Dodder Valley Park-Oldbawn Car Park 
(53°16’39.9”N 6°21’24.7”W).
These free events are open to all, offering a 
chance to learn more about biodiversity and 
to see the environmental impacts of ongoing 
initiatives in our parks.
Burial Grounds Enhancements
3,348 inspections carried out by 
our Waste Enforcement Team
SDCC plays a key role in enforcing 
national waste laws through our 
waste 
enforcement 
officers 
who 
are authorised under the Waste 
Management Act 1996 and other 
environmental legislation, to monitor 
activities including construction debris, 
illegal dumping, waste metals, end-of-
life vehicles, and the Deposit Return 
Scheme.
Last year our waste enforcement team 
conducted 3,348 inspections, handled 
408 household waste complaints, 
inspected 98 sites, and ran 7 anti-
dumping collection days, collecting 
1,341 mattresses and 8,539 kg of 
hazardous liquids for recycling and 
disposal.
Any illegal dumping or improper waste 
handling can be reported to the team 
by emailing info@sdublincoco.ie.
Ongoing improvements are being 
provided to SDCC burial grounds to 
create more respectful and peaceful 
spaces for remembrance for families 
and visitors.  These works include 
the development of columbarium 
walls, car park improvements and 
other enhancements.
Columbarium walls provide a suitable 
resting place within a cemetery for 
the placing of cremated remains 
with each columbarium wall divided 
into a number of niches which can 
each accommodate two urns of 
ashes and which have a front plaque 
provided allowing space names of 
the deceased to be engraved.  
Such features are becoming an 
increasingly common and preferred 
resting place in many cemeteries, 
accompanied by a memorial garden 
to offer a solemn and peaceful space 
for reflection.
We 
recently 
commenced 
development of a columbarium wall 
at Esker Cemetery in Lucan which 
is expected to be complete by the 
end of June following which it will 
be open to accept cremation burials 
soon thereafter.  
A similar development is also due to 
begin at Bohernabreena Cemetery 
later in the year to expand the 
interment options there following 
provision in the council’s budget this 
year to provide a columbarium wall 
there.
In addition, we will also shortly be 
upgrading the surfacing and line-
marking in the car parks at both 
Bohernabreena 
and 
Newcastle 
cemeteries.  These works are based 
on feedback from visitors who have 
requested these improvements to 
ensure a respectful and dignified 
experience at SDCC burial grounds.

Bealtaine- Celebrating Creativity in 
Older Age

and host a vibrant programme 
of 
Bealtaine 
Festival 
events 
celebrating creativity in older age. 
Libraries are offering free, inclusive 
activities including poetry, painting, 
tai chi, history talks, gardening, and 
intergenerational workshops.  Our 
Active South Dublin team are also 
hosting many events, including 
low-impact exercise classes, weekly 
walks in local parks and the  ‘Go for

for older participants, encouraging 
both physical health and social

the 
area 
continues to grow as a dynamic and 
connected place.
Local Engagement
In advance of the new library being 
delivered in Citywest, we have been 
building a local culture of learning 
and reading through increasing our 
mobile library service in the area.  
Mobile libraries made 259 visits in 
2024 alone, welcoming nearly 8,000 
visitors to ensure an established 
and engaged user base from day 
one in the new library.  In addition, 
we will undertake consultation to 
inform the final fit-out of the library 
to meet the needs and expectations 
of local residents.

South Dublin County Council’s 
2024 Annual Report reflects a 
year of achievement, innovation, 
and community engagement, 
marking 30 years of service 
since its establishment in 1994. 
With a growing population 
of over 300,000 and a strong 
commitment 
to 
inclusivity 
and sustainability, the Council 
delivered 
on 
key 
targets 
across housing, climate action, 
economic 
development, 
and 
community wellbeing.
Housing and Community
A record 774 new social homes 
were 
delivered, 
alongside 
210 long-term leases and 55 
affordable 
homes. 
Projects 
progressed 
in 
Clonburris, 
Kilcarbery, and Belgard, while 
efforts to reduce homelessness 
saw 1,245 housing allocations, 
including 267 for homeless 
households. 
Community 
facilities were developed in 
areas such as Saggart and 
Glenasmole, and €2.2 million 
was 
allocated 
under 
the 
Community Recognition Fund 
to 
support 
integration 
and 
local engagement.
Climate Action and Environment
Under the Climate Action Plan, 
energy efficiency improved by 
45.5% since 2018, with 43% 
fewer 
emissions. 
Initiatives 
included the retrofitting of 85 
homes, 1,690 LED streetlight 
upgrades, and 22.5 km of new 
cycle lanes. The Clondalkin 
Decarbonising Zone and €1.1 
million in Community Climate 
Action 
funding 
supported 
meaningful local change.
Economic Growth and Tourism
The new Local Economic and 
Community Plan was adopted, 
supported 
by 
developments 
at 
Grange 
Castle 
and 
the 
opening 
of 
the 
Work 
IQ 
Innovation Centre. The Council 
processed over 5,000 business 
grants, promoted investment, 
and 
strengthened 
business 
networks. 
New 
tourism 
strategies advanced projects 
at Hellfire, Lucan House, and 
Rathfarnham 
Castle. 
Events 
such as Tradfest and the Dublin 
Discovery Trails enhanced the 
region’s cultural appeal.
Libraries, Arts and Culture
With 
over 
1.3 
million 
transactions, the library service 
reached 
more 
than 
60,000 
active members. Programmes 
such as Library Labs, Red 
Line Book Festival, and NOISE 
Music offered diverse cultural 
experiences. The Arts Office 
supported 
local 
creatives 
through residencies, bursaries, 
and public events, while new 
initiatives fostered inclusivity 
and creativity for children and 
young people.
Planning and Infrastructure
Progress 
on 
the 
County 
Development 
Plan 
included 
approval for over 12,000 new 
homes, with 5,475 completed 
since 2022. Sustainable mobility 
was prioritised with upgrades 
to roads, bridges, pedestrian 
crossings, and school zones. 
Major enhancements to public 
spaces took place in Lucan, 
Tallaght, and Dodsboro.
Equality and Integration
The Council implemented its 
Equality and Human Rights Duty, 
expanded 
the 
Neurodiverse 
South project, and launched 
new intercultural events and 
accessibility 
improvements. 
With 52.5% female councillors, 
the Council became the first in 
the State to achieve a majority 
female membership.
Financial Management
Commercial 
rates 
collection 
exceeded 
€145 
million—a 
record—while rent and loan 
collections also improved. The 
Council continued to invest 
strategically while maintaining 
strong financial performance.

members,

in

South Dublin County.
